basics.title: How it is calculated
items: The four insurances are national pension, health (with long-term care), employment and industrial accident insurance. The employer pays all of accident insurance; the rest is shared.
Premiums are pay minus non-taxable items (such as up to 200,000 KRW of meals) times the rate, with amounts under 10 KRW dropped.
National pension has an income cap and floor (updated every July), so very high or low pay is charged within that range.
Long-term care premiums are a percentage of the health premium and are collected with it.

y2027.title: What changes in 2027
items: The pension rate rises from 9.5% to 10%, 5% each for employee and employer, on the way to 13% by 2033.
Long-term care rises from 13.14% to 13.90% of the health premium (decided Oct 30, 2026).
The health insurance rate stays at 7.19%.
A government plan would raise the unemployment insurance rate from 1.8% to 2.0%, but the decree is not amended yet. It will be applied once confirmed.

employer.title: What the employer adds
items: Besides matching pension, health, long-term care and employment insurance, the employer alone pays job stability & skills premiums and accident insurance.
Job stability & skills premiums range from 0.25% (under 150 employees) to 0.85% (1,000+ or government).
Accident insurance rates are set by industry every year; the 2026 average is 1.47%.
So an employee paid 3,000,000 KRW a month (including 200,000 KRW meals) costs the employer about 11% more, around 3.32 million KRW.

items.q: How much is social insurance on 3,000,000 KRW a month?
items.a: With 2,800,000 KRW insured pay (after 200,000 KRW meals), the 2026 employee share is 272,080 KRW a month: pension 133,000, health 100,660, long-term care 13,220 and employment 25,200. In 2027, pension rises to 140,000 and long-term care to 13,990, for 279,850 KRW.

items.q: How much does the employer pay?
items.a: The same shares plus job stability & skills (0.25–0.85%) and accident insurance (by industry, 2026 average 1.47%). For 2,800,000 KRW, under 150 employees and the average accident rate: 320,240 KRW a month in 2026, 328,010 KRW in 2027.
Yes. Pension goes from 4.75% to 5% each, and long-term care from 13.14% to 13.90% of health. Health is frozen; the employment insurance rise is only a proposal so far.
No. Non-taxable amounts such as meals (up to 200,000 KRW a month) are excluded from insured pay.
Freelancers taxed as business income are not workplace members. They pay pension and health as regional members; some service-provider occupations are covered by employment and accident insurance.
